headline: Three recognized-firm audits on record but no EVM bytecode verification possible (Bitcoin/Cosmos chain); Phase 2 re-audit confirmed but not fetched this run

findings.text: Babylon Protocol runs on Bitcoin (Taproot scripts) and a Cosmos-SDK chain (Babylon Genesis), neither of which supports EVM-style Etherscan bytecode verification. DeFiPunkd's read API covers only EVM chains (chainIds 1, 10, 56, 130, 137, 324, 8453, 42161, 43114, 59144, 81457, 534352). Bitcoin scripts and Cosmos module binaries cannot be verified via any block-explorer 'Contract Source Code Verified' indicator analogous to Etherscan. The concepts of proxy contracts and implementation contracts do not apply. This is a structural gap inherent to the chain, not a protocol failing, but it means an independent outsider cannot confirm deployed behavior via a standard explorer read.

Source repos are public under the babylonlabs-io GitHub organization (https://github.com/babylonlabs-io), with repositories including babylon, simple-staking, btc-staker, btc-staking-ts, covenant-emulator, finality-provider, and others. The Zellic Phase 1 audit (June 2024) pins exact commit SHAs for 10 repos (e.g., babylon at 8d76979ef05742206a74166c480c69b44b082798, btc-staking-ts at 6494df2b9f2c7a80578356659b1d24302e69dda2). The Coinspect Phase 1 audit similarly pins commits across the same repos. These repos were originally at babylonchain/ org and have migrated to babylonlabs-io/. Source-to-repo correspondence is supported by the audit scope tables, though no independent bytecode diff was performed in this run.

Three Phase 1 audits are publicly linked on the Babylon website and were fetched this run: (1) Zellic 'Blockchain Security Assessment' (Apr 1–May 31, 2024, report dated June 28, 2024) covering 10 repos at pinned commits — 4 findings, no critical/high; (2) Coinspect 'Source Code Audit Phase 1' (May–June 2024, report version v240805) covering 10 repos at pinned commits — 12 findings (5 medium, 1 low, 5 none, 1 caution-advised), all major issues marked Fixed by July 3, 2024; (3) Cantina Security Competition (May 28–June 24, 2024, report dated August 4, 2024) on Bitcoin Staking Scripts — 89 issues (0 critical, 4 high, 11 medium, 42 low), all cited as fixed in staking-indexer PR 124, staking-api-service PRs 161/183, covenant-signer PR 43, cli-tools PR 46, Babylon PR 679. The Babylon website also references a Coinspect Phase 2 audit PDF at docs.babylonlabs.io/assets/files/coinspect_babylon_phase_2_audit_2025_03.pdf (March 2025), confirming a Phase 2 re-audit exists, but this PDF was not fetched in this run due to fetch budget constraints.

Auditor recognition: Zellic is a broadly recognized blockchain security firm (listed in the rubric). Cantina is a recognized security marketplace platform. Coinspect is an active blockchain security firm with Bitcoin/Cosmos expertise (not in the rubric's listed firms but has a substantial public track record). All three firms independently reviewed the same Phase 1 codebase, providing corroborating coverage. Zellic explicitly notes the assessment was 25.7 person-weeks with four engineers.

Post-audit drift: The Zellic Phase 1 audit explicitly stated 'we strongly recommend a re-audit of the Phase 2 components before they go live' as significant changes were anticipated. A Coinspect Phase 2 audit exists (March 2025) per the URL on the Babylon website (coinspect_babylon_phase_2_audit_2025_03.pdf), but this PDF was not fetched in this run. The Cantina competition report (August 2024) postdates the Zellic and Coinspect Phase 1 reports and covers some of the same repositories. GitHub shows the babylonlabs-io org has 58 repositories and active development through March 2026. The repository simple-staking is now archived. The babylon Genesis chain (Phase 2) involves Cosmos module code and CosmWasm contracts (cosmos-bsn-contracts repo in Rust) that were not in Phase 1 scope and whose Phase 2 audit coverage cannot be confirmed this run.

Not applicable: Babylon Protocol does not use EVM proxy/implementation patterns. The protocol uses Bitcoin Taproot scripts (verified by consensus rules) and a Cosmos-SDK chain with Go modules. There are no proxy contracts or implementation contracts in the EVM sense. The CosmWasm contracts (cosmos-bsn-contracts) are a separate concern and no block-explorer verification for them was checked in this run.

steelman.red: The protocol runs on Bitcoin and Cosmos chains not covered by any standard EVM block explorer or DeFiPunkd's read API, making independent bytecode-level verification structurally impossible for an outsider, and the Phase 2 audit scope could not be confirmed this run.
steelman.orange: While three recognized-firm audits exist for Phase 1 and a Phase 2 follow-up audit is evidenced by URL, the protocol's Bitcoin/Cosmos deployment prevents any on-chain verification via block explorers; the Phase 2 Coinspect audit PDF was not fetched to confirm its exact scope; and the cosmos-bsn-contracts (Rust CosmWasm) introduced for Phase 2 have unknown audit coverage.
steelman.green: Three substantial audits from recognized firms (Zellic, Coinspect, Cantina) cover Phase 1; all major findings were fixed; a Phase 2 re-audit by Coinspect (March 2025) is referenced on the official website; all source repos are public under babylonlabs-io on GitHub; and a $500,000 Immunefi bug bounty has been live since September 2024.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because: the green steel-man holds for Phase 1 audit coverage and public repos, but cannot be promoted to green due to (a) structural inability to confirm on-chain bytecode verification for Bitcoin/Cosmos (V1 gap recorded in unknowns), (b) the Phase 2 Coinspect audit PDF was not fetched this run so its exact contract scope cannot be cited as evidence, and (c) CosmWasm contracts (cosmos-bsn-contracts) introduced for Phase 2 have unknown audit coverage in this run. The combination of unverifiable on-chain state and unconfirmed Phase 2 audit scope puts this squarely in orange territory. The red steel-man overstates the risk — Phase 1 audit quality is strong and the Phase 2 re-audit URL is credible — but insufficient on-chain evidence and unconfirmed Phase 2 scope prevent green.

unknowns: V1-offchain: Bitcoin chain has no Etherscan-style bytecode verification; Babylon Genesis (Cosmos) chain module verification could not be confirmed via any block explorer this run — no EVM-compatible explorer exists for these chains in DeFiPunkd's supported chainIds

V3: Coinspect Phase 2 audit (docs.babylonlabs.io/assets/files/coinspect_babylon_phase_2_audit_2025_03.pdf, March 2025) was not fetched this run due to fetch budget constraints — exact contract scope and findings cannot be cited as evidence
V3: cosmos-bsn-contracts (Rust CosmWasm, github.com/babylonlabs-io/cosmos-bsn-contracts) Phase 2 audit coverage is unknown — not confirmed in any fetched document this run
V5: Commit-level drift between Phase 1 audited SHAs and current HEAD of all 10 repos was not sampled this run; extent of post-audit code changes is not quantified
V2: No independent bytecode/binary diff was performed between audited commits and current deployed Cosmos chain binaries or Bitcoin script parameters — recorded as scope limit

protocol_metadata.about: Babylon Protocol enables native Bitcoin staking directly on the Bitcoin blockchain without wrapping, pegging, or bridging. Bitcoin holders lock BTC using Taproot scripts with a timelock/unbonding/slashing path structure, allowing their stake to provide economic security to Proof-of-Stake chains ('Bitcoin Supercharged Networks') via a covenant committee co-signing mechanism and an EOTS-based finality provider layer. The Babylon Genesis chain (a Cosmos-SDK chain) acts as the coordination layer, registering stakes and finality providers, while staked BTC remains in self-custody on Bitcoin throughout.
